rules.explanation: Tradition groups the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu and a waning Moon as natural malefics (harder, testing influences), and the rest as natural benefics (gentler, supportive ones). Mercury takes on the character of whoever it is with, becoming harsh in the company of malefics.
rules.conditions: Needs the sidereal planet positions from the chart. Traditional symbolism; not a prediction.

rules.explanation: The soul and core self, authority, vitality and the father figure; read as a royal, steady and self-defining light. Its element is fire.
rules.conditions: Needs the sidereal planet positions from the chart. Traditional symbolism; not a prediction.
rules.omitted: Source also assigns planets to castes, body descriptions, deities, tastes, fabrics and tissues; only the core significations and element are used.

rules.explanation: The mind and emotional life, nourishment and the mother figure; a ruler of feeling. Gentle and changeable, it is read as strong at night and in the bright half of the month.
rules.conditions: Needs the sidereal planet positions from the chart. Traditional symbolism; not a prediction.

rules.explanation: Courage, drive and physical energy; the commander. Fiery and decisive, it brings initiative and, under stress, conflict.

rules.explanation: Discipline, duty, delay and hard-won experience; the servant. Slow and austere, it teaches through limits and its element is air.

rules.explanation: A shadow planet read as appetite, ambition, foreign or unconventional influences and obsession. It acts like an army of unsteady force.
rules.conditions: Needs the sidereal planet positions from the chart. Traditional symbolism; not a prediction.

rules.explanation: A shadow planet read as detachment, loss of attachment, spiritual searching and sudden separation; it acts like an army that cuts through.
rules.conditions: Needs the sidereal planet positions from the chart. Traditional symbolism; not a prediction.

rules.explanation: Each planet is at its strongest, exalted, in a particular sign: the Sun in Aries (peak at 10°), Moon in Taurus (3°), Mars in Capricorn (28°), Mercury in Virgo (15°), Jupiter in Cancer (5°), Venus in Pisces (27°), Saturn in Libra (20°). Seven signs opposite is its debilitation, at the same degree. An exalted planet is read as expressing its good qualities freely; a debilitated one as strained.
rules.conditions: Needs sign and degree of each planet from the chart.

rules.explanation: A planet in a sign it rules is at home. Each also has a moolatrikona portion of a sign where it is especially steady; for the Sun this is the first 20° of Leo, for the Moon 3°-30° of Taurus, for Mars the first 12° of Aries, for Mercury 15°-20° of Virgo, for Jupiter the first 10° of Sagittarius, for Venus the first 15° of Libra, for Saturn the first 20° of Aquarius.
rules.conditions: Needs sign and degree of each planet from the chart.

rules.explanation: Planets placed in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th or 12th sign from one another are temporary friends, and those in the other signs are temporary enemies. Combined with natural friendship, this gives five relationships: great friend, friend, neutral, enemy, great enemy.
rules.conditions: Needs sign positions of all planets.

rules.concept: How much of a planet's good result is realised by dignity
rules.explanation: The tradition scales a planet's results by its placement: in exaltation the full benefit, in its moolatrikona about three-quarters, in its own sign about half, in a friend's sign about a quarter, in a neutral sign about an eighth, and little or nothing in debilitation, combustion or an enemy's sign. For harmful results the same proportions run in reverse.
rules.conditions: Needs dignity of each planet.

rules.explanation: Mercury and Jupiter are strongest in the east, the Sun and Mars in the south, Saturn in the west, and Venus and the Moon in the north. A planet in its strong direction is read as better able to deliver its significations.
rules.conditions: Needs the planet's house position (mapped from direction by the tradition's standard house-direction table, not given in this chapter).

rules.concept: Strength by time of day and lunar phase
rules.explanation: The Moon, Mars and Saturn are read as stronger at night, the Sun, Jupiter and Venus by day, and Mercury at all times. In the dark half of the month the malefics are stronger, and in the bright half the benefics.
rules.conditions: Needs birth time (day or night) and the lunar phase.

rules.explanation: Benefic planets gain strength when the Sun moves north (the northern solstice period) and malefics when it moves south.
rules.conditions: Needs the Sun's position relative to the solstices.

rules.explanation: Mars rules Aries and Scorpio, Venus Taurus and Libra, Mercury Gemini and Virgo, the Moon Cancer, the Sun Leo, Jupiter Sagittarius and Pisces, and Saturn Capricorn and Aquarius. A planet is read as comfortable and at home in the signs it rules.
rules.conditions: Needs the sign of the planet or ascendant from the chart.

rules.explanation: The signs repeat in a cycle of three kinds: movable (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn) read as initiating and active; fixed (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius) read as steady and enduring; dual (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) read as adaptable and mixed.
rules.conditions: Needs the sign of the planet or ascendant from the chart.

rules.concept: Masculine and feminine signs; harsh and gentle signs
rules.explanation: The signs alternate: odd signs (Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius) are classed as masculine and harder, even signs (Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, Pisces) as feminine and gentler. The classes describe tone, not gender of people.
rules.conditions: Needs the sign of the planet or ascendant from the chart.

rules.explanation: The text assigns the signs to the three humours in a repeating cycle of four: Aries, Leo and Sagittarius to fire-like heat (pitta); Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn to air-like restlessness (vata, as the cycle is read); Gemini, Libra and Aquarius to a mixture; Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces to water-like softness (kapha). Used only as a symbolic description of temperament.
rules.conditions: Needs the sign of the planet or ascendant from the chart.
rules.omitted: Source links these to bodily constitution; health claims are not used. The mapping as written needs checking against a scholar's reading.

rules.concept: Signs strong by day or by night
rules.explanation: Signs that rise head-first (Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Aquarius) are read as strong by day, and signs that rise back-first (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius, Capricorn) as strong by night; Pisces rises either way.
rules.conditions: Needs the sign of the planet or ascendant from the chart.
rules.omitted: Per-sign detail should be checked against a scholar's reading before use.

rules.concept: Caste, body parts and physical descriptions of the signs
rules.explanation: Not used. The chapter assigns each sign a caste, a body part and bodily features; Star Talks makes no caste, health or appearance claims.
rules.conditions: n/a
